```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
library(jsonlite)
data <- fromJSON(params$data_json, simplifyVector = TRUE)
```

**Platform:** `r data$platform`  
**Date:** `r data$date`  
**Samples:** `r length(data$samples$sample_id)`

## Plasmid detection summary

```{r detection}
knitr::kable(data$samples,
             col.names = c("sample_id", "consensus_plasmids", "circular", "detection_tools"),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

## Analysis sections

```{r sections}
sections <- data$sections
knitr::kable(data.frame(Section = sections$name,
                        Status = ifelse(sections$status == "provided_input", "Provided input",
                                 ifelse(sections$present, "Outputs observed", "No output recorded"))),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

No recorded output can mean a disabled branch or a branch gated by empty inputs;
it is not a statement that an analysis found no biological hits.

## Limitations

- TETRA composition scores are not host assignments. Uncalibrated TETRA host links are disabled after the source-host benchmark failed acceptance.

- Sequence-based circularity is predictive and should be confirmed from the assembly graph or read support.
- The circular count represents candidates, not confirmed topology. Terminal inverted repeats alone do not establish circularity; a negative circularity call does not confirm linearity.
- Plasmid calls are predictions from automated classifiers; confirm biologically important hits manually.
